claim: Q1 FY2026 was Apple's largest-ever quarter at $143,756M total net sales (+16% YoY), driven by iPhone revenue of $85,269M (+23.3% YoY, an all-time record), while Services revenue growth of 13.9% YoY was the slowest of the three FY2026 quarters reported.
stance_target: Services growth is decelerating even as the iPhone 17 supercycle accelerates hardware growth, raising the required forward Services CAGR to hold total growth flat once the iPhone cycle normalizes
scope_conditions: Q1 FY2026, three months ended December 27, 2025, vs Q1 FY2025 comparative
quoted_support: iPhone had its best-ever quarter driven by unprecedented demand, with all-time records across every geographic segment, and Services also achieved an all-time revenue record, up 14 percent from a year ago.

claim: Apple's installed base of active devices exceeded 2.5 billion units as of Q1 FY2026, per CEO Tim Cook, the disclosed proxy for the size of the annuity-like Services revenue base.
stance_target: Ecosystem lock-in scale as the structural foundation for annuity-like Services revenue durability
scope_conditions: As stated by Apple management, December 2025 quarter; company does not disclose device count in the financial statements themselves, only in prose commentary
quoted_support: our installed base now has more than 2.5 billion active devices, which is a testament to incredible customer satisfaction for the very best products and services in the world

claim: Greater China revenue surged 37.9% YoY to $25,526M in Q1 FY2026, the sharpest of the three FY2026 China growth prints, on top of a weak prior-year base.
stance_target: A persistent structural decline thesis for Apple's China revenue
scope_conditions: Q1 FY2026 only; single-quarter rebound against an easy comparison
quoted_support: Greater China 25,526 / 18,513 (three months ended December 27, 2025 / December 28, 2024)

claim: Apple returned almost $32 billion to shareholders in Q1 FY2026 alone (dividends plus buybacks) against $53.9 billion of operating cash flow generated that quarter, a shareholder-return payout ratio of roughly 59% of operating cash flow.
stance_target: Shareholder returns (buybacks/dividends) are a first-order, quantifiable component of the 2-5y total return identity, not a residual
quoted_support: These exceptionally strong results generated nearly $54 billion in operating cash flow, allowing us to return almost $32 billion to shareholders.
